title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 23-26). L is an ambient set or space. A 'figure' F in L is a set of pairwise disjoint subsets of L (cells), with support |F| = union of the cells. The set of cells I = F is ordered by an incidence relation, and the tautological map p : |F| -> I is a semicontinuous surjection: |F| carries the inverse-image topology of the Alexandrov-type topology on the poset. Concretely this is a cellular or stratified decomposition of a subset of L, and it is the combinatorial-topological skeleton of the 'tame topology' Grothendieck called for in the Esquisse.

Three relations on figures:
- F <= G: F is a subfigure, i.e. F is a subset of G as a set of cells.
- F ≼ G: F is a subdivision of G, i.e. |F| = |G| and every cell of F lies in a cell of G.
- F << G: F refines G, i.e. |F| is contained in |G| and every cell of F lies in a cell of G.

Page 24 encodes a refinement as a commutative square: S = |F| is contained in T = |G|, which is contained in L; p : S -> I and q : T -> J are semicontinuous surjections; φ : I -> J is increasing; and q∘i = φ∘p.

Page 25, first part. The subdivision case is exactly S = T. The datum then collapses to a factorisation S ->> I ->> J of the projection, with φ surjective and q := φ∘p. So a subdivision is a coarsening map of cell posets over the same support.

Marginal note (largely illegible). It warns about the case φ bijective. With S = T and φ bijective, the fibres coincide, so the cell sets coincide; distinctness could then only come from the order or topology data. It apparently also mentions the case F ≼ G with R_F = R_G (R presumably the cell equivalence relation on the support) and remarks on |F| ≠ |G|. I cannot reliably reconstruct the exact claim.

Proposition. F << G if and only if there is a subdivision G' of G with F a subfigure of G', i.e. F <= G' ≼ G. In words, refinement = subfigure-of-a-subdivision.
- Sufficiency is immediate by composing the inclusions.
- Necessity: if |F| = |G| take G' = F. Otherwise fill the gap with point-cells, G' = F ⊔ {{x} : x in |G| \ |F|}. Every cell of G' lies in a cell of G, so G' ≼ G, and F <= G'.

A crossed-out part b) tried to characterise subdivisions as maximal refinements, and was abandoned. Page 26 then draws the order-theoretic conclusion: << and ≼ are mutually determined via <=. It asks whether <= is conversely expressible through << and ≼, and checks axioms C5-C8 of an abstract 'context' (an axiomatic calculus of figures).
errors: The proof says 'on prend G' = G si F est déjà une subd.'; the correct choice is G' = F, since F <= F ≼ G. Taking G' = G gives F <= G, which is false when F ≠ G.
The index of the added singletons is transcribed / written as x in |F| \ |G|; it must be x in |G| \ |F|, the part of the support of G not covered by F.

Gap: G' = F ⊔ {singletons} is only an admissible figure if arbitrary (possibly infinite) families of point-cells are allowed, and if an order/topology can be put on G' making |G'| -> G' semicontinuous. Treating the added points as minimal or isolated cells must be compatible with the closure relations of F inside the cells of G. In any finite or tame (e.g. semi-algebraic or o-minimal) setting this construction fails, since |G| \ |F| is typically infinite, and one would need a genuine cell decomposition of |G| \ |F| compatible with F.
The crossed-out part b) (subdivision = maximal refinement) is not correct as stated, which is presumably why it was struck.

ideas.what: Encoding refinement and subdivision of cell decompositions as commutative squares of semicontinuous surjections onto posets, with an increasing map of posets
ideas.modern_name: Morphisms of stratified spaces / poset-stratified spaces (stratification as a continuous map to a poset with Alexandrov topology); refinement of stratifications
ideas.usually_credited_to: Poset-stratified viewpoint: Lurie (Higher Algebra, appendix), with earlier MacPherson and Treumann; refinement of stratifications is classical (Whitney, Thom, Mather)
ideas.where_published: Not in published Grothendieck texts to my knowledge; the Esquisse §5-6 only sketches tame topology and stratified structures

ideas.what: Refinement = subfigure of a subdivision (F << G iff F <= G' ≼ G)
ideas.modern_name: Factorisation of a refinement as a subdivision followed by restriction to a substructure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in PL topology and cell complexes

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'contexts' (C5-C8) for an algebra of figures with three interlocking order relations
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic tame topology; comparable in spirit to o-minimal structures / cell decomposition axioms
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay-Steinhorn, Knight (1984-86); van den Dries' book 1998
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme (1984) announces a tame-topology program but does not contain these axioms

missed.claim: This page belongs to Grothendieck's 1986 attempt at an axiomatic 'algebra of figures': abstract contexts with relations <=, ≼, << and axioms C5-C8. It is an unpublished concrete realisation of the Esquisse's tame-topology program, developed in the same years as, and independently of, o-minimality. This particular page only contains a routine lemma.
missed.quote: Pour que F raffine G, il faut et il suffit que F soit une sous-figure d'une subdivision G' de G ; F ≤ G' ≼ G
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Comparing Grothendieck's order-theoretic axioms for figures with o-minimal cell decomposition and with poset-stratified homotopy theory could reveal an alternative axiomatisation of tame geometry. That comparison is not in the literature, but the content of this page alone is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is an elementary order-theoretic lemma about cell decompositions, with a small slip in the proof. The interest lies only in its place within Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic tame-topology project, which is historically notable but not revealed in depth here.
transcription_corrections: 'x ∈ |F|_K' and '⊔_{x∈|F|∖|G|}' should both be read as x ∈ |G| ∖ |F|; the singletons fill the part of |G| not covered by F.

'(surj. [?] ..., surj. loc fin.) ⇒ id.' at the top likely ends the previous page's sentence about direct images of closed parts under surjective, locally finite maps; it probably reads '(surj. propre?, surj. loc. fin.) ⇒ id.'.
'factorisation [?]' is plausible; it is written as 'factorisation' just above the diagram S ↪ L, p↓surj I, φ↓surj J.
In the margin, 'F ≼ G i.e. R_F = R_G' seems to involve F ≼ G together with G ≼ F (or φ bijective); the note is too illegible to transcribe reliably.
'Dém. [?] la condition suffisante, I [?]' probably reads 'Dém. La condition suffisante est triviale. Inversement, supposons F ≪ G'.
